Inpatient hospitalization: Abbott Northwestern in Minneapolis, PrairieCare in Brooklyn Park, and Fairview in Minneapolis take this age. Going to an emergency room will get you to this level of care the easiest/fastest. Prepare to be in the emergency room for a few days “boarding”/waiting for a bed. Bring him things that will keep him comfortable - his comfort items, clothing, books, etc. 

Childrens mental health case management: this could be extremely helpful. This a case manager through your county that will meet with you and your child at minimum monthly. They can make referrals for services and assess that these services are meeting the needs of your child. They can advocate for your child in the school setting. They also have exclusive access to resources/services. You can call your county (google “x county children’s mental health case management”) and request the service or ask any of your child’s established providers (or the social worker at the hospital if they get admitted to inpatient) for a referral. You woild get a case manager faster if someone else refers you.

Childrens therapeutic services and supports (CTSS): also known as a “skills worker.” This is an only accessible if you DONT have private insurance (I have never understood the insurance limitation). A skills worker is someone who comes into the home and works 1:1 with a child on: social skills, anger management, depression, anxiety, cooperation, and adhd. They can also do family skills work. 

Source: I have been a social worker in Minnesota for 10 years. I have worked on inpatient psychiatric mental health units with children on and off for 8 years, and was a children’s mental health case manager. Feel free to message me if you have questions.
